answer: Each agent locks a stake before its quill may sign an attestation, and validators slash that stake when one identity votes twice. Honest signatures ripple outward as reputation, so trust accrues only to the staked signer. To pass off a raven swarm of fake identities, an attacker must fund one full stake per clone; doubling votes doubles the capital at risk, and detected duplicates are burned. Flooding a quorum therefore costs far more than casting the single honest vote it tries to outweigh.
